summary: The shared live-volume material now applies its solver-owned wet-bank vertex coverage to Single Layer Water scattering, absorption, and behind-water color as well as surface opacity. Zero-coverage bank vertices therefore carry no residual optical water volume and return the dry scene to identity instead of leaving a low-opacity pale rail. All five river-local live-water instances consume the updated versioned parent. This closes a material-graph ownership defect but does not pass photoreal review: the matched Chilko frame still contains a broad pale shallow-water transition, Futaleufu remains overbright and sheet-like, and the surrounding terrain, vegetation, foam, spray, and atmosphere remain procedural.

root_cause.prior_surface_contract: The procedural core wrote smooth station/lateral wet coverage to vertex alpha, and the shared parent multiplied ordinary surface opacity by that coverage.
root_cause.missing_volume_contract: Single Layer Water evaluates scattering, absorption, and behind-water color independently of ordinary opacity. Those terms stayed fully active where vertex alpha approached zero, so geometry and opacity work could not completely remove the pale rectangular optical rail at the sampled bank.
root_cause.retained_solution: Multiply scattering and absorption by the existing coverage expression and blend ColorScaleBehindWater from identity to its authored response with the same coverage in the versioned shared parent.
root_cause.authority_boundary: The material consumes existing presentation vertex alpha only. It cannot add a wet vertex or triangle and changes no sampled wet/dry mask, cooked field, terrain, bank geometry, bathymetry, collision, navigation, buoyancy, raft force, breaking-site authority, D3, D4, score, or progression state.

chilko_bank_closeup.diagnostic_region: columns 700-1239, rows 340-419; first blue-minus-red > 8 shoreline sample per column
chilko_bank_closeup.visual_verdict: Retain only as complete optical-coverage semantics. The detected water boundary changes without exposing a dry gap, detached island, black edge, or outward water expansion. The broad pale shallow-water tone transition remains obvious, so this frame does not support photoreal shoreline acceptance or a claim that final bank naturalism is solved.

futaleufu_breaking_water_side.visual_verdict: No new bank hole, hard rail, black boundary, detached water body, or rapid-face discontinuity appears. The broad overbright analytical breaking body is unchanged in character and remains photoreal-rejected.
